head2head_summary_note: Commit-then-Steer strictly dominates Native GS, Official PGID-F, and SEAL across matched cohorts and operating points, now backed by standard MS-COCO-1K FID/CLIP (vs Real-5K: sscd_64b 52.97->52.17, hyb 53.02->52.98; 1,000-image Clean blind joint 97.3%/97.2%) and statistically significant N=10 Live 151-step Imprint tests (Cross-Prompt: Commit-Steer 0/10 vs Native GS 10/10 [p=1.08e-5], SEAL @4 6/10 [p=0.0108], PGID-F >=167 5/10 [p=0.0325] / default 2/10; vs PGID-F also 5.1x faster verify, +16.3pp 9-GS on matched-30, Reprompt+ 2/108 vs 104/108; vs SEAL dominates across all 3 40k-calibrated points @12/@4/@2 where SEAL suffers robustness collapse at @12 [9-GS 45.6%, Regen-4 26.3%] and forgery collapse at @4/@2 [Imprint 6-7/10, Proxy Reprompt 16-26/36, target regen 10-15/18]). Against Paper-faithful SemBind GS-S (matched-20 & N=10 Imprint; 4-carrier full matrix incl. GS++ and authors' private training/binding code remain outside released scope), Stage 4D+5B/5C+6B establish a statistically significant architectural Pareto boundary: Commit-then-Steer wins training-free, 3.0x faster gen, 11.7x faster verify, instance-preserving low-drift trajectory, zero-shot SDXL/PRC transfer (incl. SDXL Live Imprint 0/4 vs 4/4), AND same-prompt instance-level security (N=10 Same-Prompt Imprint sscd_64b 3/10 [p=0.0031], hyb 5/10 [p=0.0325] vs SemBind 10/10 [all 30/30 ckpts BA=1.0000]; Same-Prompt Reprompt+ hyb 2/24, sscd64 9/24 vs SemBind 24/24), whereas SemBind GS-S retains higher harsh-occlusion 9-GS survival (93.9% vs 81.7%), higher strong diffusion-regeneration joint survival (80/80 vs 65/80; Commit-Steer 192b auth is 80/80), and 0/72 cross-prompt Reprompt+ at >181/256.
evaluation_policy: Unchanged published top-venue author attacks only; full budgets; no adaptive or improved attacks; independent null calibration and evaluation; report achieved FPR and absolute TPR.
